pencereler.0-5: Two hundred thousand miles from Earth, an oxygen tank exploded. In seconds, Apollo 13
pencereler.5-12: lost most of its power and oxygen. So how did a tank that passed every test just explode? Its
pencereler.12-20: heater switches were rated for 28 volts, not 65. They welded shut, and wires inside cooked at a thousand degrees. Weeks later,
pencereler.20-30: in space, damaged wiring sparked inside pure oxygen. The crew survived using the lunar module as a lifeboat. One mismatched voltage nearly cost three lives.

segmentler.metin: Apollo 13 lost an oxygen tank 200,000 miles from Earth.
It took only heater switches rated for 28 V run on 65 V.
So how could heater switches rated for 28 V run on 65 V do this?

The answer is thermostat switches welded shut by overvoltage, overheating the tank's wiring insulation — and it is why every component rating is now checked against every power source it will ever see, including ground equipment.
